svg.title: One pass of an always-on review agent
svg.desc: Left: six things that changed on a pull request since the last pass. A label, a passing check, a bot comment and a review request are read without waking the model; a maintainer's review comment and a new commit wake it. In the replays, 42% of passes with a change woke no model. Right: the agent is handed its note on the thread, what it said there before, only the news, and the diff saved to a file. Claude Code runs once with read-only tools in the clone and no GitHub token, and ends with a reply for the outbox, a question, or nothing; nothing is posted until a maintainer sends it. Measured on 76 merged pull requests from five repositories against an agent that rereads everything and keeps no memory: 0.52 times the cost, 0.41 times the drafts and 0.78 times the reviewer points raised first.
